title: Shout out to the entire @The Notebook Tour cast but especially Alysha...
transcript: Last night I spontaneously bought tickets to the notebook tour again, except now we're in Denver and I got a last minute ticket for $47. It is listed as partial view, but it is in the second row. To be honest though, it's a better view than when I sat front row on Broadway cause I'm a little further back. I don't think that's gonna be that partial view, to be honest. If there's anything on that side of the stage, I won't be able to see it. But as far as I remember from the tour, most everything takes place in the centre. It is intermission. Oh my gosh, I am so happy to see everybody really settle into these roles. They are so good. And the vocals at high altitude. I'm shook, I'm shook! Woo hoo! I love this show so freaking much. I have loved it in every single iteration, but it is so much fun to get to see this cast, like really, really get comfortable with these roles and find their stride. They've truly found it. I I had an absolute blast. I'm so glad I got to see this show again. I will probably be back before this run ends, but it is here for another week in Denver until December 28th. And it's just fantastic. And also the partial view seats are not partial at all, so by all means buy them. They're cheap and a really, really, really great view. And the way That you're sitting on the side, you get to see, like, all of their micro expressions, especially all of the Noahs, because from where I was sitting, that's mostly who I got to see the react reactions of. But, like, all three of the Noahs had the best reactions to Ali, which was just incredible. Especially Beau Gravitte, who plays the older Noah, had this expression on his face when older Allie was, like, playing the notes on the piano, and just the. The absolute devastation and the heartbreak on his face was. Ah, it was so good. I love this show so much, and I'm so glad it's on tour, and you should go see it. And if you're in Denver, you have another week.
